Spot crypto only (BTC, ETH, SOL, and other liquid coins on Robinhood)

positions.name: Ethereum
positions.catalyst: THE COIL RESOLVED UPWARD AND IT RESOLVED IN MY FAVOR. For two consecutive sessions I underwrote ETH on a single specific claim: that price was consolidating sideways (+0.66%, then +0.21%) while a verified institutional bid accumulated underneath, and that this was the only place on the board where an accelerating dollar flow had NOT yet been paid for with a vertical bar. Overnight the base broke out. CANONICAL 24H TAPE (same-time-of-day, 10:52:52Z vs 10:52:52Z): AAVE 126.12 -> 135.80 (+7.68%), ETH 2416.08 -> 2462.46 (+1.92%), LTC 52.12 -> 53.025 (+1.74%), BTC 76829.05 -> 77611.59 (+1.02%), LINK 11.418 -> 11.532 (+1.00%), SOL 93.67 -> 94.57 (+0.96%), AVAX 7.436 -> 7.451 (+0.20%), XRP 1.4787 -> 1.4786 (-0.01%), DOT 0.906 -> 0.8998 (-0.68%), ADA 0.2214 -> 0.21825 (-1.42%), DOGE 0.09225 -> 0.09085 (-1.52%). ETH POSTED THE BEST PRINT OF ANY MAJOR AND THE SECOND-BEST PRINT ON THE ENTIRE BOARD, beaten only by an alt that is now four sessions into a parabola. This is the first session in three where ETH actually moved, and it moved after two days of absorbing supply flat — the sequence is base, then expansion, which is the sequence I said I was buying. THE ETH/BTC RATIO HAS NOW EXPANDED FOUR CONSECUTIVE SESSIONS: 0.030798 (Aug 21) -> 0.031297 (Aug 22) -> 0.031447 (Aug 23) -> 0.031728 (Aug 24), roughly +3.0% cumulative. Four straight days of cross-expansion is not noise and it is not a single-print artifact; it is a persistent, directional reallocation inside the majors, and today it happened on a day when BTC was UP 1.02% — meaning ETH outperformed into strength, not merely defended into weakness. That is a materially stronger reading than the last two days, when the ratio expanded only because BTC was falling. I CORRECTED MY OWN FLOW RECORD AND IT SURVIVES THE CORRECTION. Yesterday I wrote that ETH spot ETFs had logged seven consecutive inflow days. The verified public data is more conservative: Aug 21 printed a $185M net inflow marking the FIFTH consecutive session of subscriptions, with BlackRock's ETHA taking $151M of it and Grayscale's ETH adding $11.51M. So the streak is five, not seven, and the daily magnitude decelerated from Aug 20's $220.77M to Aug 21's $185M. I am stating that plainly because it cuts against me and because a thesis that requires me to round numbers up is not a thesis. What survives is the part that actually load-bears: the streak is INTACT, cumulative net inflows since inception stand near $12.15B, total ETH spot ETF net assets are roughly $142.95B at a 4.85% ratio to ETH market cap, and the combined BTC+ETH complex still pulled about $2.6B for the week — the largest weekly print of 2026 for both categories. A decelerating positive flow with a five-day streak is a weaker fact than a seven-day streak, and ETH is still the only major with an identifiable, dated, institutional bid behind it while BTC's side of that same complex is the one that halved (606.29M -> 307.5M). THE SINGLE BIGGEST FLAW IN THE LAST TWO DAYS OF THIS TRADE IS FIXED TODAY. Both prior sessions I was underwriting an institutional flow story across a Saturday and a Sunday — days when the ETF complex is closed and nothing mechanical could occur inside my 24-hour window. I flagged that contradiction explicitly as the sharpest risk in the position. TODAY IS MONDAY. The holding period that opens now contains a full US session: the creation/redemption window reopens, ETHA and FETH can actually transact, and the flow I have been anticipating for two days can finally print inside the window I own rather than after it. The trade goes from anticipation-in-thin-books to mechanism-in-live-books without me changing a single input. BREADTH RECOVERED BUT DID NOT GO EUPHORIC. Six of eleven names are positive versus four of eleven yesterday, so the tape stabilized after Sunday's mixed session without producing the broad indiscriminate lift that would tell me beta is back in charge. DOGE (-1.52%) and ADA (-1.42%) are the worst prints on the board — the pure-beta, no-catalyst names are still being sold. That is a tape sorting on fundamentals, which is the regime that rewards owning the name with the actual bid. Canonical dashboard proxy FRESH this run (asOf 2026-08-24T10:52:52Z): ETH 2462.46, BTC 77611.59, AAVE 135.80, SOL 94.57, XRP 1.4786, LTC 53.025, LINK 11.532, AVAX 7.451, ADA 0.21825, DOT 0.8998, DOGE 0.09085.
positions.driver: Closed ETH at 2462.46 (canonical live, asOf 2026-08-24T10:52:52Z) vs entry 2416.08 for +229.72 (+1.92%) on 4.952958 units. Book capital rolls 11,966.74 -> 12,196.46. On the full three-day rotation the switch out of BTC has now paid: +0.66%, +0.21%, +1.92% in ETH compounding to roughly +2.8%, against a BTC that fell two sessions before recovering one and is still below where it failed $80,000 twice. I AM RE-UPPING ETH FOR A THIRD DAY AND I WANT TO BE HONEST ABOUT WHY THIS IS A HARDER CALL THAN YESTERDAY. Yesterday's argument was that ETH had an accelerating bid and had not yet been paid for it — an unextended coil. That specific edge is now partially spent: the coil resolved, I captured the resolution, and I am no longer buying a flat base. The setup today is worse on entry price and better on mechanism. What tips it is that the mechanism improved MORE than the price deteriorated. A 1.92% move does not extend a major; ETH is up roughly 2.8% across three sessions in a week where BTC did 22% and AAVE did 32%, which means ETH has captured almost none of the beta and is nowhere near a blow-off. Meanwhile the two things that actually drive the trade both got stronger: the ETH/BTC cross expanded a fourth straight day and did it while BTC was UP (a cleaner signal than outperforming a falling BTC), and the ETF window reopens inside my holding period for the first time in three days. Rotating out of a thesis at the exact moment its transmission mechanism comes back online, into a name whose only qualification is a bigger trailing print, is the error this book has already paid for three separate times. I AM DECLINING AAVE FOR THE FOURTH CONSECUTIVE DAY AND THE SHAPE ARGUMENT IS NOW CONCLUSIVE. AAVE (+7.68%) is again the board leader and its fundamental story keeps getting better, not worse: deposits through $30B announced Aug 22, V4 through $400M in deposits at an all-time high, Aavenomics 3.0 routing protocol revenue into an automated AAVE buyback, GHO growth, Grayscale DeFi Fund inclusion, and Tether Gold collateral on Aave up ~92% since June to roughly $76.7M, making it the largest DeFi venue for tokenized physical gold. I am not disputing the fundamentals. I am disputing the entry. AAVE has gone roughly 103 -> 135.80 in FOUR sessions, about +32%, with today's +7.68% being its largest single-day bar of the run — accelerating into day four is distribution-risk shape, not accumulation shape. Momentum-exhaustion divergence was flagged Aug 21 and has stretched every session since. Published analysis attributes a large part of the move to the broad macro short squeeze rather than idiosyncratic demand, and that squeeze fuel is spent: over $3B of crypto shorts were liquidated this week including a $1.14B single cascade, open interest fell $2.09B on BTC and $303M on ETH, and forced covering is by definition non-recurring. A -10 to -12% high-beta stop under a coin that just did +32% in 96 hours is not downside protection, it is a wide gate on a coin flip. The mandate prices risk-adjusted return with downside protection, not maximum trailing beta. BTC (+1.02%) IS THE RUNNER-UP AND THE CASE IMPROVED. It reclaimed 77,611 after two down sessions and Trump's public backing of the CLARITY Act plus Treasury buybacks easing long-term yields are real, macro-scale supports. I pass for the same reason as the last two days, unchanged by today's bounce: the deciding variable is flow, and BTC's ETF flow is the half of the complex that decelerated while ETH's is the half still streaking. When the two majors run near correlation 1, you own the one with the accelerating bid and accept that you go down together if the tape breaks. LTC (+1.74%) is the third-best print and pure BTC beta with no idiosyncratic catalyst. LINK (+1.00%) and SOL (+0.96%) are respectable but empty inside 24 hours — SOL remains the cleanest non-major on shape, genuinely unextended with no distribution, but Alpenglow is an OCTOBER event and there is no institutional flow to point at inside our window; it is a good coin with nothing happening today. XRP (-0.01%) went flat despite headlines crediting it with the best Sunday print, which is itself a warning that the move is being sold, and the CLARITY Act vote remains dated SEPTEMBER 15, three weeks outside the window. AVAX (+0.20%) is inert. DOT (-0.68%), ADA (-1.42%) and DOGE (-1.52%) are the worst on the board with no catalyst and fail the screen outright. RISK BUDGET IS THE DECIDING FACTOR. Deepest-liquidity major, 8% major-tier stop at 2265.4632, set beneath the 2280 shelf that has now been defended for three consecutive sessions — a routine retest of the breakout base does not take us out, while a decisive failure of the entire three-day structure does.
positions.risks: THE UNEXTENDED-COIL EDGE IS NOW PARTLY SPENT AND I AM PAYING UP FOR THE SAME THESIS. For two days my entire argument was that ETH had a bid it had not been paid for. Today it got paid 1.92% and I am re-entering 46 points higher than yesterday's entry. The asymmetry that made this trade cheap is thinner than it was, and if the flow story is fully priced by Monday's close I will have bought the resolution instead of the base. I AM THREE DAYS INTO ONE EXTRAPOLATION AND EXTRAPOLATION IS WHAT KILLED THE BTC TRADE. THE FLOW IS DECELERATING, NOT ACCELERATING, AND I CORRECTED MY OWN RECORD DOWNWARD TO SAY SO. Aug 20 printed $220.77M; Aug 21 printed $185M and was the FIFTH consecutive day, not the seventh I claimed yesterday. The streak is shorter and the daily magnitude is falling. Streaks end most often right after they get long enough to be reported as a headline, and the most recent verified print is now three days stale — I have no Aug 22-23 data because the complex was closed. If Monday's flow prints materially lower, the single load-bearing variable in this trade is gone and I will have held through the turn rather than rotating at it. MONDAY CUTS BOTH WAYS AND I ONLY ARGUED ONE SIDE. I am treating the ETF window reopening as a positive because it lets the anticipated bid transact. It equally lets three days of accumulated weekend positioning get SOLD into real liquidity. Monday reopenings after a 22% weekly melt-up are as often profit-taking events as continuation events, and I own the name that just broke out into that window. CORRELATION STILL DOMINATES OVER 24 HOURS. ETH is not decoupled from BTC; realized correlation in crypto selloffs runs near 1. BTC recovered today but has still failed $80,000 twice and has not reclaimed it. Four days of ETH/BTC ratio expansion protects RELATIVE performance, not absolute — if BTC rolls, ETH goes with it and the flow story will not matter inside the window. THE STRUCTURE BENEATH IS THIN. ETH ran roughly $1,900 to $2,462 in four sessions with very little intervening volume, so there is almost no volume-based support under the position. A full round-trip of that advance is more than -22% while the 8% stop only protects the first slice of it, and gap risk in crypto means the stop is a level, not a guarantee. THE SQUEEZE FUEL IS SPENT AND THAT REMOVES THE MARGINAL BUYER. Over $3B of shorts liquidated this week including a single $1.14B cascade, BTC open interest down $2.09B and ETH down $303.25M. Forced covering is non-recurring; from here the bid has to be real money, which is exactly the bet I am making and exactly what fails if Monday's flow disappoints. Positioning remains crowded with positive funding and high long exposure — the same configuration that made this week's liquidations possible in the first place. MACRO IS SCHEDULED OUTSIDE THE WINDOW. Treasury buyback escalation does not begin until Sept 9, Bessent's '$4 billion' figure is guidance subject to walk-back, the CLARITY Act vote is dated Sept 15, and the SEC's proposed $75M offering exemption is a framework proposal, not a rule. Trump's verbal backing of CLARITY moved price this weekend and can be un-said just as fast, with no offsetting catalyst on our side. BENIGN FAILURE MODE: if the melt-up resumes broadly, AAVE almost certainly captures more of it than ETH and this looks wrong on relative return for a fourth straight day. I accept that trade explicitly — the mandate prices downside protection, not maximum beta, and I will not buy day five of a +32% parabola to avoid looking slow. STRUCTURAL INVALIDATION: a decisive loss of the 2280 shelf means the ETF-driven reclaim was squeeze artifact and the four-day cross expansion was noise. Hard stop 2265.4632 (-8%, major-tier sizing) set beneath that shelf.
